chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd al-Madāʾinī, from Muṣaddaq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār ibn Mūsā, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, concerning:
If a man trims his nails with iron, or cuts some of his hair, or shaves the back of his neck, then he must wipe it with water before he performs salat (prayer).

He was asked: then if he has performed salat (prayer) and did not wipe any of that with water? He said: he repeats the salat (prayer), because iron is impure. And he said: because iron is the attire of the people of the Fire, while gold is the attire of the people of Paradise.

So the proper way regarding this report is that we carry it upon a mode of recommendation rather than obligation, because it is an anomalous report that contradicts the many reports; and whatever proceeds in this manner is not acted upon, as we have explained.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةَ: salat (prayer), the act whose validity is discussed here
key_terms.الِاسْتِحْبَابِ: recommendation, the juristic interpretation given in the closing statement
key_terms.الْحَدِيدِ: iron, mentioned here in relation to trimming and a claimed ritual effect
key_terms.الْمَاءِ: water, used here for wiping before salat (prayer)
key_terms.شَعْرِهِ: his hair, referring to cutting or trimming hair
key_terms.نَجَسٌ: impure, the stated rationale within the report
key_terms.يَمْسَحَهُ: wipe it, meaning to pass water over the affected area

ai.seo_question: Is it obligatory to wash or wipe with water after using iron to cut nails or hair before salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This report discusses wiping with water after using iron to trim nails or cut hair before performing salat (prayer), and it mentions repeating the prayer if that was not done. However, the closing statement clarifies that this report is to be understood as recommending the act rather than making it obligatory, because it is anomalous and conflicts with numerous other reports.
